question.knowledge_point: Finding a Position Vector Given an Acceleration Vector
question.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},0⟩\,,\,t\in (0,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(2,3)$ and has velocity $⟨1,-1⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},0⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})\text{d}t,\int 0\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t}+{C}_{1},{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨1,-1⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨\frac{1}{1}+{C}_{1},{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,-1⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=-1.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨\frac{1}{t},-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{t},-1⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{t}\,\text{d}t,\int (-1)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t+{C}_{3},-t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(1)=⟨2,3⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡1+{C}_{3},-1+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨2,3⟩ & =⟨{C}_{3},-1+{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{3}=2$ and ${C}_{4}=4.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2+\operatorname{ln}⁡t,4-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
